mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which can lead to increased borrowing and investment, thereby driving up S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not positively correlated with the federal funds rate decline, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests a weakening labor market, which could negatively impact consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns despite a rising unemployment rate above 5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When employment (PAYEMS) increases but the unemployment rate (UNRATE) also rises, it may indicate structural imbalances in the labor market, potentially leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive despite the described labor market conditions, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, rising federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, which can negatively impact corporate profitability and lead to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns remain positive during a period of rising federal funds rates above 4%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which can boost corporate revenues and lead to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative despite increasing retail sales, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) may signal reduced economic activity, leading to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive despite a decline in industrial production below 95, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is strong but accompanied by rising federal funds rates, it may indicate inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive despite the described conditions, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, low unemployment (UNRATE) may lead to wage inflation, increasing labor costs and potentially reducing corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns remain positive during a late-cycle expansion with low unemployment, this hypothesis is rejected.
